create.name: Marc Lesser
create.bio:
Marc Lesser is a Zen priest who brings meditation into working life. He spent ten years living at San Francisco Zen Center and served as director of Tassajara, its mountain monastery, before taking an MBA and starting and running several businesses. He helped create Search Inside Yourself, the mindfulness and emotional intelligence course first taught inside Google, and was the founding chief executive of the institute that grew from it; today he runs ZBA Associates, a leadership development firm.

His teaching joins sitting practice with everyday questions of work, conflict and relationships. He hosts Mill Valley Zen, a free weekly online sitting group with a talk and discussion, leads half-day retreats in Mill Valley, two-month practice periods online and residential practice periods at Green Gulch Farm, and offers a year-long one-to-one mentorship for leaders as well as recorded audio courses. He presents the Zen Bones podcast, and his five books run from Z.B.A., an early look at business as practice, through Less and Seven Practices of a Mindful Leader to Finding Clarity, on compassionate accountability.

books.title: Finding Clarity: How Compassionate Accountability Builds Vibrant Relationships, Thriving Workplaces, and Meaningful Lives
books.author: Marc Lesser
books.description: His most recent book offers a practice he calls compassionate accountability: a way of naming tension and difficult conversations honestly while keeping care for everyone involved, at work and at home.

books.title: Seven Practices of a Mindful Leader: Lessons from Google and a Zen Monastery Kitchen
books.author: Marc Lesser
books.description: Seven practices for leading with presence, drawn from his years in a Zen monastery kitchen and in teaching mindfulness at Google.

books.title: Know Yourself, Forget Yourself
books.author: Marc Lesser
books.description: A book that applies Zen practice to the way we work and relate, balancing self-knowledge with letting go of a fixed sense of self.

books.title: Less: Accomplishing More by Doing Less
books.author: Marc Lesser
books.description: An invitation to do less of what is unnecessary, using simple contemplative practice to find more room and focus in a crowded life.

books.title: Z.B.A.: Zen of Business Administration
books.author: Marc Lesser
books.description: His first book looks at running a business as a form of practice, bringing Zen attitudes to work, money and decisions.

courses.title: 2-Month Practice Period: Zen in Everyday Life (online)
courses.description: Weekly Thursday evening online meetings for two months, each opening with lightly guided meditation, to begin or deepen a sitting practice and carry it into work and home life.

courses.title: 3-Week Practice Period at Green Gulch Farm
courses.description: A residential Zen practice period at San Francisco Zen Center's Green Gulch Farm, with daily zazen, work practice, study and one-to-one meetings with him, ending in a five-day sesshin. Registration is through the Zen Center.

courses.title: Zen of Leadership: A Year of Transformation
courses.description: A year of one-to-one mentoring with Marc for leaders and others who want a steady personal meditation practice and clearer values in how they live and lead.

courses.title: Seven Practices of a Mindful Leader – Guided Audio Course
courses.description: A seven-week audio course on his seven practices, with guided exercises on awareness, communication and trust, for leaders at any level.

free_resources.title: Mill Valley Zen weekly meditation group
free_resources.description: A free weekly online sitting led by Marc: half an hour of meditation, then a talk or discussion. Open to beginners; donations welcome.

free_resources.title: Mill Valley Zen guided meditations
free_resources.description: Recorded guided meditations from his weekly group, on themes such as letting go and cultivating appreciation.

free_resources.title: Zen Bones podcast
free_resources.description: His podcast of conversations and short practices on bringing old contemplative wisdom into modern work and life.
